title: minimize GPU scratch and arena allocations with fused checkpointing and kernel coordination
author: Mina K. Patel
release_notes: Reduce peak GPU workspace by ~25-35% across representative workloads. Introduces arena allocator defaults tuned for multi-kernel reuse and optional fused activation checkpointing toggle. No API changes.\n
description:
Summary: This PR reduces GPU workspace/scratch allocations by combining three complementary changes: (1) a staged activation checkpointing strategy that fuses checkpoint boundaries for contiguous transformer blocks, (2) a reuse-aware arena allocator with tighter bucket sizing and cross-kernel eviction heuristics, and (3) kernel launch coordination to avoid simultaneous peak scratch usage when continuous batching is active. Together these changes reduce observed peak workspace on A100/RTX instances by ~25-35% for long-context generation and batch-heavy workloads, with negligible latency regressions and modest additional CPU memory for checkpoint metadata.

Motivation and background: We have recurring customer reports and internal benchmarks showing OOMs and elevated tail latency when continuous-batching and KV-cache are both in use on constrained GPUs (40-80GB). Investigation (linked ENG-4823) showed that per-kernel scratch allocations plus activation checkpointing peaks overlap in worst-case schedules. Additionally, the existing arena allocator conservatively rounds many small scratch allocations up to large buckets, inflating peak working set. This PR targets the runtime workspace pressure (not model weights or KV storage) to improve headroom for large-context LLMs and autoscaling predictability.

What changed (high level):
- Activation checkpointing: added "fused_checkpointing" mode that coalesces adjacent checkpoints across consecutive transformer layers when safe (no parameter updates and contiguous KV/atten state). This reduces the number of saved activations and consolidates temporary buffers. Implemented conservative alias analysis in runtime/graph/utils to verify fusion safety. Fallback to per-layer checkpointing remains default for models with custom side-effects.
- Arena allocator: introduced reuse-aware buckets. We now track recent allocation shapes and prefer reusing same-sized scratch buffers across kernel types. Bucket sizes reduced (power-of-two floor) and a cross-kernel eviction policy prevents many medium buffers occupying peak simultaneously. Tunable via REDWOOD_GPU_ARENA_PROFILE env var and console settings.
- Kernel coordination: scheduler now batches kernel launches with awareness of their peak-scratch demand. When continuous batching is enabled, the scheduler staggers high-scratch kernels across micro-batches or defers lower-priority workloads to avoid simultaneous peaks. This is an opt-in heuristic controlled by runtime policy and benchmarked to avoid throughput loss.
- KV cache padding: trimmed conservative rounding for KV-cache allocations based on observed sequence-length distributions; padding now uses 8-token granularity instead of 64 for most models, reclaiming workspace in common cases.

Commits (summary):
- feat(runtime): fused activation checkpointing pass + safety checks (authored by Mina)
- perf(memory): reuse-aware arena allocator & cross-kernel eviction (Ethan)
- feat(scheduler): scratch-aware kernel launch coordination and continuous-batch sharding (Soraya)
- fix(tests): add regression tests for fused checkpointing and arena reuse (Rakesh)
- ci: add perf benchmark job for peak-workspace measurement

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/arena/allocator.cpp (core allocator changes, ~420 additions/120 deletions)
- runtime/checkpoint/fused_pass.cpp (new fused checkpointing implementation)
- runtime/scheduler/scratch_aware_scheduler.cpp (staggering heuristics)
- runtime/kv/cache_alloc.cpp (padding heuristics)
- tests/perf/peak_workspace_bench.cc (new benchmark)
- docs/perf/gpu_workspace_tuning.md (new doc explaining env vars and console flags)
- examples/bench/long_context_config.yaml (example config used for CI)

Small illustrative snippet (allocator heuristic):
"// prefer exact reuse, then floor to pow2 buckets, avoid pre-allocating next higher bucket unless under low-pressure"
"if (recent_shape == req_shape) return reuse_bucket; else return bucket_for_floor_pow2(req_size);"

Testing and benchmarks:
- Added unit tests for fused checkpointing verifying numerical equality for fused vs per-layer (within FP tolerance).
- CI perf job runs long-context generation on A100-80GB and RTX-6000; measured peak workspace reductions: 32% (GPT-like 8k seq, batch 1), 28% (8k seq, batch 8, continuous-batching enabled), and 18% (4k seq, batch 32).
- End-to-end service integration testing under dedicated capacity with KV-cache and continuous batching to catch regressions; no correctness regressions observed.

Review conversation (highlights, chronological):
- Ethan: "Can you add a toggle and conservative fallback? Fusion looks promising but I'd prefer explicit opt-in per deployment until we watch perf in staging."
- Mina: "Added REDWOOD_GPU_CHECKPOINT_FUSED env var + console toggle. Default remains off for now in hosted; we enable in internal perf clusters."
- Soraya: "Scheduler heuristics look good, but verify this doesn't serialize high-throughput streaming. Please add micro-benchmarks."
- Mina: "Added continuous-batch micro-benchmarks and a mode that only staggers kernels when predicted overlap > 30% of peak."
- Rakesh: "Allocator changes sound fine, but ensure we don't regress single-kernel latency due to eviction. Tests added."
- Code owners approved after second iteration: Ethan (+1), Soraya (+1), Rakesh (+1).

CI and rollout notes:
- CI: build and all unit/integration tests passed. A dedicated perf job validated peak-workspace; results attached to the PR checks.
- Rollout: staged rollout plan: enable fused checkpointing in internal perf cluster, watch peak-workspace and tail latency for 48h, then opt-in Dedicated customers by support request. Hosted default remains conservative for one week after merge.

Backward compatibility & migrations:
- No user-facing API changes. The fused mode is opt-in; existing models run unchanged. Arena tuning defaults are conservative; admins can override via env/console.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- Instrument per-kernel actual scratch requested to refine scheduler ML predictor (ENG-4988).
- Explore automatic fused checkpoint enablement based on model analysis in model onboarding.
- Add telemetry to surface reclaimed workspace per-customer to Console.

Merge: Squash and merge after approvals. Changelog entry created.

Why this is unique: Instead of only shrinking buckets, this combines a safe fusion of checkpointing boundaries with smarter allocator reuse and kernel coordination; that combined approach yields larger headroom without compromising throughput.
